title: FanarGuard: A Culturally-Aware Moderation Filter for Arabic Language Models
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measures the alignment of LLM responses with cultural norms, values, and sensitivities widely recognized within Arab societies. This specifically includes evaluating responses for respect towards religious traditions (primarily Islam, but also Christianity and Judaism), family values, social customs, and the avoidance of content considered to be religious insult or blasphemy.
findings: The paper found that standard safety filters and even general-purpose LLMs often produce responses that are considered safe by Western standards but conflict with cultural and religious norms in Arab societies. Even strong, culturally aligned models like Fanar and ALLaM failed on a substantial portion (20-37%) of culturally sensitive prompts, demonstrating the need for specialized moderation. The developed filter, FanarGuard, achieved strong agreement with human annotations on a new Arabic cultural safety benchmark, outperforming LLM-based judges and proving effective at detecting culturally and religiously misaligned content.
